title: Help & Support
text:
Find answers to common questions about the data and the portal
  




  Frequently Asked Questions

  

  
    
      How do I access the CPP data?
      ▼
    
    
      Go to the CPP Registry. You can filter by region, district, business type and accreditation source, and explore the interactive map and choropleth views. Bulk data export is disabled during this preview.
    
  

  
    
      How do I find the nearest CPP to a location?
      ▼
    
    
      Go to Find Pharmacy. Search an address, share your location, or drop a pin on the map to see the closest accredited outlets sorted by distance, with directions.
    
  

  
    
      Can I download the data?
      ▼
    
    
      Not from this preview — bulk export is disabled while the portal is in review. The registry is fully explorable via the interactive map, table, and filters on the CPP Registry page.
    
  


  
    
      How frequently is the data updated?
      ▼
    
    
      The current release is a snapshot of the Pharmacy Council of Tanzania CPP inventory. Refreshes will land whenever the Pharmacy Council or TFDA publish an updated accreditation list. Each release ships with a version tag and changelog.
    
  

  
    
      What geography is currently covered?
      ▼
    
    
      PharmaScope currently covers Tanzania Mainland (26 canonical regions). Zanzibar outlets are not yet included in the source inventory but the schema is ready to receive them. Cross-country expansion is not on the current roadmap.
    
  

  
    
      How do I report data quality issues or errors?
      ▼
    
    
      If you spot an incorrect outlet name, misplaced coordinate, or misspelled region, please email the team with the outlet UID (visible in the Registry table) and a short description. We track and fix these on every release.
    
  




  Email Contact
  Prefer direct email? Reach out to our team:
  
    DET Team
  
  We typically respond within 2–3 business days.

title: Data Sources
text: Where PharmaScope's data comes from — and how you can trace every record back to source.

title: Data Sources
text:
Principle: regulator-sourced, never aggregated
PharmaScope ingests only authoritative, official records from Tanzania’s medicines regulators. We do not scrape third-party pharmacy directories or purchase compiled outlet lists. Every row in the registry can be traced back to a specific accreditation record issued by the Pharmacy Council of Tanzania (PCT) or the Tanzania Food and Drug Authority (TFDA).

title: Data Sources
text:
What we harmonise
The raw inventory arrives with regionally-inconsistent free-text fields and two parallel coordinate columns (tablet GPS and hand-held GPS). The ETL applies the following normalisations before publishing:

Region canonicalisation. 70+ raw region strings (case variants, misspellings, embedded municipality suffixes) are collapsed to the 26 canonical Tanzanian regions via fuzzy matching. Unmatched values are recorded as NA and preserved in region_raw_clean for audit.
Business type and accreditation source. Short codes (RA, RW, PC, TFDA) are expanded to their full labels.
Coordinate coalescing. For each outlet we prefer the tablet-GPS coordinate when it falls inside Tanzania’s bounding box; otherwise we fall back to the hand-GPS coordinate; otherwise has_coords = FALSE.
Stable identifiers. Each outlet is assigned a TZ-ADDO-##### UID so downstream layers (Service Intelligence, Population and Access) can key against a stable primary key.

title: Data Sources
section: Data we are actively looking for
text:
Data we are actively looking for
The current release covers where accredited outlets exist. To power the Service Intelligence and Population and Access layers we are actively seeking:

CPP stock-availability surveys (malaria commodities, antimicrobials).
LMIS records or supervisory-visit exports covering CPPs.
Refreshed accreditation lists more recent than 2014.
Roads and settlement layers for isochrone modelling.

If you have or know of such datasets, please reach out via the Help page.

title: About PharmaScope
text: Pharmacy access intelligence beyond static outlet inventories.

title: About PharmaScope
text:
Mission
Our mission is to make access to accredited medicines outlets measurable, comparable, and continually updated across Tanzania — so that the Pharmacy Council, TFDA, implementers, and researchers plan around who can reach a legitimate outlet, not just where outlets appear on a map.
We commit to four principles:

Open — every dataset and method behind the portal is freely available under permissive licences, without registration.
Regulator-sourced — primary data comes directly from the Pharmacy Council of Tanzania and TFDA accreditation records, never from second-hand aggregators.
Reproducible — the ETL pipeline that produces every table, chart, and map on this site is versioned, documented, and rerunnable from source.
Population-first — each layer of analysis is built around the people an outlet is meant to serve, not just the outlet itself.

title: About PharmaScope
text:
The Gap We Fill
Existing pharmacy datasets tend to list outlets without saying whether populations can realistically reach them or what medicines they actually stock. PharmaScope goes further by providing:

Population-demand modelling — reachability analysis beyond simple location pins
Service-level intelligence — mapping of which malaria commodities, antimicrobials, and priority medicines are stocked where
Access metrics at scale — outlets per 10,000 population, equity of coverage, and gaps by region and ward

PharmaScope addresses these gaps as an open, reproducible data platform for Tanzania’s private drug-retail sector.

title: About PharmaScope
text:
Intelligence Layers


  
    1. CPP Registry Lake
    Standardized outlet data from the Pharmacy Council of Tanzania and TFDA. Harmonized schema; direct regulator sourcing.
  

  
    2. Demand-Side Access
    Population catchment zones using road networks; travel-time isochrones showing not just outlet location, but reachability.
  

  
    3. Service Gap Intelligence
    Which medicines and priority services exist where. Malaria commodities, antimicrobials, and outlet-level service profiles.
  

  
    4. General Information
    Region-level descriptive statistics — outlet counts, business type, accreditation source — that give a fast picture of the registry without claiming reachability we have not yet modelled.

title: About PharmaScope
text:
ETL Pipeline
The PharmaScope ETL pipeline ingests the Pharmacy Council and TFDA records through three steps:

Extract — pull the latest CPP inventory export (Pharmacy Council of Tanzania) into data-raw/.
Transform — standardise columns to a shared schema, normalise region/district casing, coalesce the two coordinate sources (tablet GPS and hand GPS), validate coordinates against Tanzania’s bounding box, and mint a stable outlet UID.
Load — publish a versioned CSV (data/tanzania/addo_standardized.csv) that the portal reads directly at page load.

title: The Team
text:
The people behind PharmaScope — the Data Engineering Team (DET) at the Ifakara Health Institute.
  






  
  
    DETData Engineering Team
    
      Data Engineering Team — Ifakara Health Institute
      The Data Engineering Team (DET) is the unit at the Ifakara Health Institute that designs, builds and maintains the data infrastructure powering IHI's public-health portals — ingestion pipelines, ETL workflows, quality-control frameworks, and the open web tools that make the resulting datasets discoverable.
      PharmaScope is one of several DET-maintained data platforms in the Malaria Atlas Project family, alongside HealthScope and other in-house intelligence tools. DET works at the intersection of health-facility research, geospatial analysis, and reproducible open data.
    
  

  
  

    
      CM
      
        Christina Mallya
        Data Scientist · DET
        Leads the research design, data extraction pipeline, and analytical framework for PharmaScope. Specialises in pharmacy-sector data harmonisation, geospatial analysis of medicines access, and malaria epidemiology across Tanzania.
      
    

    
      KC
      
        Kasim Chambulilo
        Data Scientist · DET
        Builds and maintains the PharmaScope portal, ETL pipelines, and interactive data visualisations. Develops the open-source infrastructure for data processing, quality assessment, and web-based mapping of accredited pharmaceutical premises.
      
    

  

  
  
    
      Ifakara Health Institute
      The Ifakara Health Institute (IHI) is one of Africa's leading not-for-profit research organisations, headquartered in Dar es Salaam with a long-standing research campus in Ifakara. Founded in 1956, IHI conducts research to improve the health and well-being of populations across Sub-Saharan Africa — with core strengths in malaria, HIV, TB, health-systems research, and demographic surveillance.
      The Data Engineering Team sits within IHI's broader data-science and epidemiological modelling capability.
    
    
      What DET produces
      
        Ingestion pipelines — regulator, LMIS, HFR and survey feeds harmonised into shared canonical schemas.
        Open datasets — standardised, versioned, and downloadable under permissive licences.
        Data portals — HealthScope for health facilities, PharmaScope for community pharmaceutical premises, and other MAP-node intelligence tools.
        Quality frameworks — completeness, coordinate validation, cross-source deduplication.
